translations.text: Paul, a prisoner of Jesus Christ, and Timothy our brother, to Philemon, our beloved friend and fellow worker,
and to Apphia our sister, and Archippus our fellow soldier, and the church in your house.
Grace to you and peace from God our Father and from the Lord Jesus Christ.
I thank my God at all times, remembering you in my prayers,
when I hear of your faith and the love you have for the Lord Jesus and for all the saints,
so that the sharing of your faith may become valuable through the knowledge of every good thing that is among you in Christ Jesus.
I have received great joy and comfort from your love, because the hearts of the saints have been refreshed through you, brother.
Therefore I have great boldness in Christ to command you to do what is right.
Instead, I appeal to you on the basis of love, being such a person as Paul, an old man and now also a prisoner of Jesus Christ.
I appeal to you for my son Onesimus, whom I fathered while in chains,
who was once useless to you, but is now useful both to you and to me.
I have sent him to you, and you should receive him—that is, my own heart.
I wanted to keep him with me so that he might serve me in your place while I am in chains for the gospel.
But I did not want to do anything without your consent, so that your good deed might not be forced, but voluntary.
Perhaps he was separated from you for a time for this reason: so that you might have him forever,
no longer as a slave, but more than a slave, as a beloved brother. If he is this to me, how much more so to you, both in the flesh and in the Lord!
If you consider me your partner, receive him as you would receive me.
And if he has wronged you in any way or owes you anything, charge that to me.
I, Paul, have written this with my own hand: I will repay it—not to mention that you owe me your very self.
Yes, brother, let me have this benefit from you in the Lord; refresh my heart in Christ.
Confident of your obedience, I have written to you, because I know that you will do even more than I say.
At the same time, prepare lodging for me, because I hope that through your prayers I will be granted to you.
Epaphras, my fellow prisoner in Christ Jesus, sends you greetings.
And Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, and Luke, my fellow workers.

The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit.
To Philemon and Apphia, the masters of Onesimus, and to Archippus, deacon of the church of the Colossians. Written from Rome by the hand of Onesimus the slave.
